newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Gold price slide seen carrying into Europe, U.S.
newsitem.headline: Gold price slide seen carrying into Europe, U.S.

text.p: Gold prices continued to fall early afternoon trading in Australia, with widespread expectations of further declines later in the European and U.S. trading day, bullion dealers said on Monday.
Spot gold sank to around bid US$318.50 by around 0400 GMT (2.00 p.m.) after opening at around US$321.00 an ounce as stop-loss orders were systematically triggred, the dealers said.
"We're just waiting to see how much of hit it will take later today," a dealer for an international bank in Sydney said.
"In a word, Japanese stop losses," said another bank dealer
Japanese sellers were evident due to a surge in the yen against the U.S. dollar on Monday, the dealer said.
"The Japanese bought some gold on the back of comments gold prices would bottom and near-term the yen has favoured better against the U.S. (dollar) and they are getting slammed," another dealer said.
The Japanese currency by early afternoon on Monday had gained about 1.5 yen against the U.S. dollar to be 112.56/61 at 3.35 p.m. (0535 GMT).

Gold has plummeted to 12-year lows following heavy selling linked to the Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA) announcement last week that it had sold 167 tonnes of gold over six months in favour of government securities backed in foreign currencies.
Most dealers see further deterioration in the gold price, although the sentiment is not universal.
"Some funds may say we're happy with what we've got, we've got the last fifty bucks out of gold," said a Melbourne dealer.
"Let's just go buy some puts (options) at US$280 (an ounce).
However, one dealer said it was doubtful there would be sufficient support to "take the spin out of the train."
Gold was holding at around US$321 during most of the midday session, before losing further ground to the stop loss selling.
The Australian central bank sales served as the catalyst for selling gold, although dealers noted the market has been bearish for some time.
The sales by the RBA equated to sales of about 25,000 ounces a day compared with a global daily turnover of five million ounces, dealers noted.
Australian gold miners are particularly exposed to the falling gold price given the strength of the Australian dollar to the U.S. dollar.
At the current price of A$430.02 an ounce quoted by the Perth Mint, a significant number of gold mining companies have operating costs that exceed the current price.
